title: Ossie values-search and shelf filter literals are not injectable on backslash-escaping warehouses (MySQL/MariaDB)

criteria.given: an authenticated caller sends a hostile q to GET /ai/ossie/values/search
criteria.then: the search term is never inlined into SQL: buildValuesSearchSql emits a bind placeholder (LIKE ?) and runValuesSearch executes a PreparedStatement with the pattern bound as a parameter

criteria.given: a shelf filter value contains a backslash and the warehouse JDBC URL is a MySQL/MariaDB (or any unknown, backslash-escaping) dialect
criteria.then: OssieShelfSqlTranslator refuses it with IllegalArgumentException instead of folding it into a quote-doubled literal that Calcite re-emits to the warehouse verbatim

criteria.given: the warehouse is a known standard-conforming dialect (PostgreSQL, DuckDB/Quack, H2, SQL Server, Oracle)
criteria.then: backslash filter values keep working unchanged

criteria.given: OssieQueryService executes or previews a shelf query
criteria.then: it passes the connection's warehouse JDBC URL to the translator so the dialect decision is made per connection
tests ship for the bound values-search against a live Calcite/H2 schema with hostile input, the dialect classifier, and the translator backslash guard
